tools.name: list_zones
tools.description: List the DNS zones you can read, with their provider folder (EuroDNS folders, "/" for a zone in no folder) and counts of managed, foreign, tainted and pending RRsets. Zones flagged unmanaged exist in a provider account but are not managed by the gate: their RRsets are readable (list_rrsets, get_rrset) but cannot be changed or adopted until a policy administrator brings them under management. Optional filter on a folder glob.

folder.description: optional EuroDNS folder glob: /ES is the folder ES only, /ES/** every folder below it, / the zones in no folder

tools.name: list_rrsets
tools.description: List the RRsets of a zone, URL forwards included (type URLFWD), with their owner team and ownership status (managed: owned by a team through the gate; foreign: created outside the gate, read-only; tainted: changed outside the gate, writes blocked; pending; missing), and the tombstones: RRsets deleted recently, reserved for their team until they expire. Optional filters on status, host glob, type and owner team.

host.description: host glob relative to the zone, * matches any characters, @ is the apex

status.description: filter: managed, tainted, pending, foreign or missing

zone.description: zone name (managed or unmanaged), e.g. example.com

tools.name: get_rrset
tools.description: Get one RRset (values, TTL, owner team, status; for type URLFWD the URL forward of the host and whether forwards answer HTTPS), its tombstone when it was deleted recently, whether and why you may change it (ownership), and its recent audit history.

host.description: host relative to the zone, @ for the apex

tools.name: search_audit
tools.description: Search the gate audit log, newest first. Only events of zones you can read are returned. Use next_cursor to page.

subject.description: partial, case-insensitive match on the subject or its name

tools.name: list_teams
tools.description: List the teams that own RRsets: declared in the policy, referenced without being declared, derived from claims (families), or only found in the ownership store, with their roles and the number of RRsets they own in the zones you can read. Your own teams are in the teams field of the answer, your default team (the one new RRsets go to) first.

tools.name: get_team
tools.description: Describe a team: description, origin, members (with policy.read), roles and their rules per zone (with policy.read or as a member), RRsets and tombstones it owns per readable zone, and its pending transfers.

team.description: team name, as listed by list_teams

tools.name: check_propagation
tools.description: Check whether an RRset of a managed zone is visible in the DNS: asks the authoritative name servers of the zone and public resolvers around the world, and compares each answer with the RRset as read from the provider. Per server: status (match, stale: other values or TTL still cached, missing: no record, error, indeterminate: alias addresses not tied to the target), values, remaining TTL and latency; summary.converged is true once every server that answered matches, an authoritative one at least, and summary.max_ttl_left bounds when stale caches expire. After apply_rrset_change, pass the new_hash of the change as expect (absent after a deletion). Resolvers keep the previous answer until its TTL runs out: check again later rather than in a loop (results are cached for a few seconds and checks are rate limited).

expect.description: optional content hash just written (new_hash of apply_rrset_change), or absent after a deletion: the check is refused when the RRset still differs after a fresh provider read

host.description: host relative to the zone, @ for the apex
